prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1277; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Received first notice of loss for side impact collision at signalized intersection. Insured reports other vehicle entered on red. Police report requested. Claimant reported neck strain at scene and transported by ambulance to local hospital for evaluation.

Entry 2: Claimant is represented by counsel. All further contact to go through attorney's office. Letter of representation on file. Requested medical records and itemized bills through counsel. Liability appears clear based on insured's statement and two independent witness accounts, pending review of signal timing data.

Entry 3: Obtained copy of responding officer's report. Officer documented right-front damage to insured vehicle and left-side damage to claimant vehicle. Diagnosis from treating provider noted as cervical strain with prescribed physical therapy. Reviewing treatment plan for reasonableness and relation to the collision.

Entry 4: Counsel submitted demand package including treatment summary and wage loss documentation. Requested an additional period of records from prior primary care provider to review pre-existing neck complaints. Set reserve for bodily injury pending completion of medical review. Scheduled recorded statement with claimant through counsel.

Entry 5: Reviewed photos of both vehicles and repair estimates. Recorded statement completed with claimant's attorney present. Claimant describes ongoing neck stiffness and headaches, limited to moderate in severity. Referred file to supervisor for settlement authority review and noted next follow-up on outstanding records.
